page.layout: One printed page, one column of lexicon entries. Each entry opens with a Hebrew headword, some in large type hanging at the left. No marginal notes. Page number at the top right. Running head at the top centre. Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: תָּכַךְ m. תּוֹךְ תֹּךְ [?] Dolus, Fraus, Psalm.55.12. & 72.4. & 10.7. Quidam deducunt à תָּוֶךְ, quòd Intra hominem concipiatur.
תִּכּוּיִם m.pl. Calliditates, Industriae fraudulentae: רָשׁ וְאִישׁ תַּכְּנִים [?] Pauper & vir industriarum, Prov.29.13.
תּוּכִיִּים, תֻּכִּיִּים [?] f.p. Pavones, vel juxta quosdam, Plittaci [?], 1.Reg.10.22. 2.Par.9.21.
תְּכֵלֶת f. Hyacinthus; & metonymicè, Hyacinthinum, Exod.26. & 35.

תָּכַן Expendit, Perpendit, numero & pondere. Part. תּוֹכֵן רוּחוֹת Perpendens spiritus, Proverb.16. v.2. וְתֹכֵן לִבּוֹת Perpendit animos, Proverb.21.2. Niph. נִתְכַּן Aptari, Disponi, Rectificari, Rectum, Æquum, Conveniens esse. Affine Verbo כּוּן. Praeterit. וְלֹא נִתְכְּנוּ Et non aptantur, 1.Sam.2.3. ubi Masorethae legendum tradunt וְלוֹ Et ipsi. Futur. וְלֹא יִתְכֵּן Non est aequa via Domini, Ezech.18.v.29. יִתְכְּנוּ Recta erunt? Ibid. Pih. Praeterit. וּשְׁמַיִם בְּזֶרֶת תִּכֵּן Et coelos palmo expendit, Jesa.40. v.12. מִי־תִכֵּן Quis expendit, verf.13. וּמַיִם תִּכֵּן Et aquas appendit, Job.28.25. תִּכַּנְתִּי Aptavi, Direxi, Psal.75.4. Pyh. Partic. כֶּסֶף הַמְתֻכָּן Pecunia appensa, 2.Reg.12.11.
תִּכֶּן Summa, Demensum, Mensura: תִּכַּן אֶחָד Mensura unius, Ezech.45.11. וְתִכַּן Et summam, Exod.5.18.
מַתְכֹּנֶת f. Summa, Mensura, Forma, Dispositio; וְאֶת־מַתְכֹּנֶת Et summam laterū, Exod.5.8. Aff. עַל־מַתְכֻּנְתּוֹ In formam suam, 2.Paral.24.13.
תַּלְּג [?] m. Chald. Nix: כְּתַלְגָּא חִוָּר [?] Ut nix album erat, Dan.7.v.9. Ab Hebraeo שֶׁלֶג, mutato pro more ש in ת.

page.notes: Scan is low resolution. Hebrew vowel points and consonants are read from the image with doubt, especially headwords and the Chaldee form in the entry for the word meaning nix. Marked [?]: first headword, Hebrew phrases in the entries for תִּכּוּיִם, תּוּכִיִּים (the Latin word "Plittaci" may be "Psittaci"), תִּכְנִיר, and the last entry's headword and Chaldee phrase. The Hebrew catchword תלח is read clearly.
